The AI Adoption Partner is a hands-on AI delivery role where progress is measured in hours and days, not months and years. Our AI is delivered through a defined, sanctioned toolset and inside a clear governance envelope, not through open experimentation with whatever tool is fastest to hand.

Embedded in the business rather than in IT, each AI Adoption Partner finds where AI genuinely moves the needle for their cluster, builds it using internal and external tools and makes sure it is adopted, measured and where it works, spread to the rest of the Group.

The role has three equally weighted objectives: make K3 more efficient; create new or better value for clients; and improve colleagues' working lives by removing repetitive, low-value work. It sits at the intersection of three things that must move together - the Group AI & Data Strategy, the pace the business wants to move at and the obligations (cyber, data and regulatory) K3 already carries as a professional services group.


Why this role is different

This is a live build role inside a Group that has already done the strategic groundwork: an approved AI assistant (Aimee), an approved no-code build environment (Claude Artifacts), a Group AI & Data Strategy and a Cyber Security Strategy already in flight. The AI Adoption Partner does not start from a blank page, they start from a governed platform and a live strategic portfolio, and their job is to turn that into delivered, measured value inside their cluster.

Success is tangible and is tracked centrally: time released, stronger client outcomes, new revenue, reduced risk, and a measurably better colleague experience.


Operating boundaries — what “responsible and fast” means here

Speed in this role comes from working inside a known toolset and a known governance model, not around one. Every AI Adoption Partner works within:

  • Approved toolset only: Aimee and Claude Artifacts. No shadow AI, personal AI accounts, or unapproved frontier-model access.

  • K3's AI Policy and “Golden Rule,” data protection obligations and professional / client confidentiality duties, applied from the first prototype not at go-live.

  • EU AI Act obligations relevant to K3's dual provider / deployer status, including mandatory risk-tiering of any new use case before it touches live client or candidate data.

  • Cost governance: all model usage routed and monitored under the Group's model-routing policy.


Person specification

Essential

  • Proven use of AI and generative AI to deliver measurable business outcomes, ideally including a named conversational AI assistant and a no-code AI build tool (e.g. a Copilot-class assistant, Claude Artifacts/similar).

  • End-to-end delivery experience: problem definition, prototyping, rollout and adoption.

  • Able to understand a business problem quickly and turn it into a working solution at pace, inside a defined toolset.

  • Sound working knowledge of data protection, client confidentiality and responsible AI in a professional or regulated environment; able to apply a risk-tiering process without being told each time.

  • Clear communicator, credible with partners, fee-earners and support teams alike.

  • Curious and adaptable, willing to challenge established ways of working while maintaining trust, professional judgement and toolset discipline.

Desirable

  • Professional services or regulated-advisory experience.

  • Change, product, process-mapping or lean delivery experience.

Job Description

The Senior Data Scientist turns complex and often loosely defined business questions into clear, actionable insight. The role leads high-value analytical work using Python, SQL, statistical methods and appropriate machine-learning techniques to explain what is happening, understand why it is happening and assess what may happen next. The jobholder combines analytical rigour with commercial judgement, stakeholder engagement and strong written communication, ensuring that analysis results in practical business decisions.

The kind of person we are looking for 

Curious, commercially minded and highly analytical. The successful person will be equally comfortable working in Python, SQL and statistical models, sitting with a senior stakeholder to clarify an uncertain question, and stepping back to explain the “so what?” in plain language. Most importantly, they will create clarity from ambiguity, work at pace and turn analysis into decisions. 

Competence, knowledge and skills

Essential

  • Significant experience as a Data Analyst, Senior Data Analyst, Data Scientist, Insight Analyst or equivalent analytical professional.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to create clarity from ambiguous business questions.
  • Advanced Python skills for data analysis and modelling, together with strong SQL capability.
  • Practical experience applying statistical and data-science techniques to business problems, including several of forecasting, regression, classification, segmentation and propensity modelling.
  • Sound understanding of statistical concepts, model evaluation, uncertainty, bias and the limitations of analytical approaches.
  • Experience working with large or complex datasets and performing data discovery, validation and exploratory analysis.
  • Excellent requirements-gathering, stakeholder-management and project-planning skills.
  • Excellent written communication, with experience producing analytical papers or recommendations for senior audiences.
  • Ability to translate complex analysis into concise conclusions, commercial implications and practical actions.
  • Ability to iterate quickly, prioritise effectively and provide useful initial answers without waiting for perfectly defined requirements.

Desirable

  • Experience with time-series techniques such as ARIMA, exponential smoothing or related forecasting methods.
  • Experience developing customer churn, lifetime value, propensity, anomaly-detection or segmentation models.
  • Experience analysing financial, operational, customer or risk data.
  • Experience using machine-learning techniques beyond traditional statistical analysis.
  • Experience with Snowflake or another cloud data platform, Streamlit, and Power BI
  • Experience in financial services or another regulated, data-rich environment.

The role

You'll work across a mixture of new development and existing production systems.

A typical project could involve understanding an operational problem, working out how the underlying systems and data need to interact, building the solution and then taking responsibility for getting it safely into production.

The environment covers application development, APIs, relational databases, integrations, automation and AI-enabled workflows. You won't be boxed into purely front-end or back-end development.

AI development tools are already part of the team's engineering workflow. You'll use them to accelerate development, but you'll still be responsible for the quality of what gets released. The business wants developers who understand the difference between using AI productively and blindly shipping generated code.

What you'll be doing

You'll design and develop internal applications, automated processes and integrations between business systems.

That will include working with APIs and webhooks, manipulating data held in relational databases and developing services that move information between different applications.

You'll also help develop AI-enabled processes used by operational teams. Some will run automatically; others will require appropriate checks or human intervention.

Once something goes live, it remains an engineering responsibility. You'll be involved in testing, releases, monitoring and troubleshooting production issues.

When something breaks, you'll need to be comfortable following the problem through several layers — application, API, integration and database — rather than assuming the problem belongs to somebody else.

What we're looking for

You'll already have commercial software development experience and be comfortable working across several parts of an application.

You'll need:

  • Strong relational database and SQL skills.
  • Experience developing and integrating APIs.
  • Experience working with third-party systems and integrations.
  • A good understanding of data structures and how information moves between applications.
  • Experience working across both front-end and back-end development.
  • Practical experience using modern AI development or coding tools.
  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience supporting software running in production.
  • An understanding of testing, source control and software release processes.
  • The ability to turn a business requirement into a practical technical solution.
  • Enough independence to take a piece of work from initial discussion through to release.

The technology

The team works with a mixture of Python and modern web technologies, alongside APIs, workflow automation and established business applications.

You don't need to have worked with every technology in the environment.

What's more important is that you've built real software, understand databases and integrations, and can get up to speed with an unfamiliar system without needing everything documented for you.

Experience with workflow automation, CI/CD, authentication, desktop applications or cloud-based business systems would all be useful.

The person

You'll probably enjoy this role if you're interested in what happens when software meets actual business operations.

The technical challenge isn't simply writing code. It's understanding how people use a process, where the data comes from, what other systems depend on it and what happens when something fails.

It's a relatively small development environment, so you'll have genuine ownership of your work. You'll need to be comfortable making decisions, investigating problems and pointing out when an existing process could be improved.

You should also have a sensible attitude towards AI. The business is investing in it and wants to move quickly, but reliability still matters. Knowing when automation needs controls, checks or a human involved is part of the job.

The National Haemophilia Database (NHD) is the UK's national registry for people with inherited and acquired bleeding disorders, collecting clinical and treatment data from NHS haemophilia centres across the UK.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Clinical Research Data Manager to provide specialist data management and coordination for post-marketing studies, investigator-initiated studies and other approved research delivered through the NHD.

Working with clinicians, NHS haemophilia centres, researchers and external study partners, you will translate study protocols and research questions into practical data-collection requirements. This will include developing study-specific Case Report Forms (CRFs), database modules, worksheets, data management plans and completion guidance.

You will also be a key operational contact for participating centres, helping sites meet study requirements and ensuring research data are complete, accurate, timely and suitable for analysis and reporting.

The role covers three main areas:

  • Clinical research data management - developing study data-collection tools and processes and coordinating data review, cleaning, validation and query resolution.
  • Site coordination and training - supporting participating NHS centres and providing practical guidance and training on study requirements and data submission.
  • Research governance and quality - ensuring study data management meets applicable research governance, data protection, consent and quality-assurance requirements.

You will join the established UKHCDO/NHD multidisciplinary team, working alongside data managers, data scientists, statisticians and clinicians, and with external partners including pharmaceutical companies and Clinical Research Organisations (CROs).

Key Responsibilities:

Clinical Research Data Management:

You will:

  • Lead the design, review, piloting and implementation of paper and electronic CRFs, worksheets and study-specific data-collection tools.
  • Translate study protocols, endpoints and research questions into proportionate, clinically meaningful data fields and collection processes.
  • Develop and maintain data management plans, data dictionaries, CRF completion guidance and associated documentation.
  • Coordinate the collection, entry and verification of clinical research data from participating sites.
  • Review data for completeness, consistency and accuracy, managing data cleaning and query resolution.
  • Monitor data quality, completeness, timeliness and site performance.
  • Support the development and maintenance of NHD databases and study-specific modules, recommending improvements to systems and processes.

Site Coordination and Training:

You will act as a principal operational contact for participating centres, building effective relationships with Haemophilia Centre Medical Directors, Research Nurses, Data Managers and other clinical and research staff.

You will establish practical data-collection arrangements, provide training and guidance on study requirements and CRF completion, respond to operational and system queries, and work collaboratively with sites to overcome barriers to high-quality and timely data collection.

You will also liaise with external study partners and CROs, attend relevant study meetings and coordinate agreed actions.

Research Governance and Quality:

You will apply a sound working knowledge of UK research governance, HRA and Research Ethics Committee requirements, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and sponsor responsibilities.

You will ensure appropriate compliance with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and NHS information-governance requirements, maintaining confidentiality and appropriate management of personal data.

You will support safety-reporting and quality-assurance processes and ensure study documentation is accurate, complete and appropriately version controlled.

You will also contribute to team meetings, procedures, policies and service improvements, using a proactive and practical approach to solving problems and improving clinical research data management.

About You:

We are looking for someone who combines strong clinical research data-management skills with the ability to work effectively with busy NHS clinical and research teams.

Essential Requirements

You will have:

  • A degree in life sciences, health sciences, data management or a related subject, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
  • Current Good Clinical Practice (GCP) training.
  • Substantial experience in clinical research, clinical data management or study coordination.

Business Systems Analyst

Job Overview

Open House Estate Agents Bolton is a well-established residential and commercial estate agency, providing property sales, lettings and property management services across Bolton and the surrounding area. Our team handles the full customer journey, from first enquiry through to completion, and we rely on consistent systems and accurate data to keep that process running smoothly. We are looking for a Business Systems Analyst to take ownership of the systems, data and reporting that support our sales, lettings and property management operations, working closely with our sales, lettings and accounts teams to keep case progression, compliance prompts, communication logging and record retention all working reliably.

Responsibilities

Own analysis of workflows across sales, lettings and property management cases, identifying duplication, delays and control gaps, and delivering improvements

Gather requirements directly from senior management and operational/finance leads, and translate these into system configurations, templates and process controls that fit real day-to-day operations

Configure, maintain and continuously improve our core business systems, including the CRM platform, to keep case stages, task ownership, communication records and reporting fully auditable

Use CRM and reporting data to identify growth opportunities and support business development into new areas and services

Build and maintain structured management information and operational reporting, giving pipeline visibility, task status, workload oversight and service performance indicators to support decision-making

Lead controlled change delivery: scope and test system and process changes, roll them out with minimal disruption, and maintain a clear change log

Support monthly financial and sales reporting, reconciling data between the CRM and accounts systems to catch and resolve discrepancies early

Support budgeting, forecasting and cash-flow reporting through the systems and data you manage

Support SEO and digital marketing reporting, tracking website performance and lead-generation trends to inform business decisions

Train and support staff across the business on correct system use, embedding consistent adoption and reducing reliance on manual workarounds

Experience

Degree in Business, Finance, IT, Data or a related discipline, or equivalent demonstrable professional experience gained in a fast-paced operational role

1–3 years' experience in a business systems analyst, business/data analyst, or process improvement role, or equivalent demonstrable experience

A proven track record of configuring and administering CRM or case-management platforms end to end, not just using one day to day

Comfortable working with financial and sales data, with the analytical rigour to spot and resolve reconciliation issues

Advanced Excel and reporting skills, comfortable building dashboards, KPIs and management information from scratch for a busy management team

Some exposure to SEO, digital analytics or website performance tools (e.g. Google Analytics, Search Console) is a plus

Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including experience training non-technical staff and supporting adoption across a team

Good financial awareness, able to look across the business and spot opportunities to reduce costs and improve efficiency

Data Analyst


Greater Manchester | Hybrid role (2-3 days on-site)


An established and highly successful digital business is looking for a Data Analyst to join its technology team, taking ownership of reporting and analytics across a platform used by millions of people.


This is a great opportunity for someone with a couple of years' commercial data experience who enjoys getting beyond simply producing reports. You'll work with large datasets, help the business understand how its customers behave, analyse the impact of product changes and experiments, and turn complex information into clear, useful insights.


A key part of the role will be bringing greater consistency to how data is used across the organisation. You'll help create a reliable single source of truth for key metrics, build and maintain dashboards, and make it easier for teams across the business to make informed decisions without multiple people extracting and interpreting the same data in different ways.


What you'll be doing

You'll work across a broad range of data and analytics projects, including:

  • Building and maintaining dashboards and regular business reporting
  • Using SQL to query and analyse large datasets
  • Presenting analysis in a clear and accessible way to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Analysing customer behaviour across the company's digital products
  • Measuring the impact of new products, features and pricing changes
  • Analysing results from A/B tests and experiments run through the company's internal experimentation platform
  • Identifying trends, unusual behaviour and opportunities within the data
  • Helping establish consistent KPIs and reporting across the organisation
  • Supporting product and commercial teams with ad-hoc analysis
  • Developing your knowledge of web analytics and Google Analytics
  • Over time, exploring more sophisticated statistical modelling and other ways of extracting value from the company's data


What we're looking for

You don't need to be an expert in every area. We're looking for someone with a solid grounding in data analysis who is curious, commercially minded and comfortable investigating a problem rather than simply being told which report to produce.

You'll ideally have:

  • Commercial experience working as a Data Analyst, Product Analyst, BI Analyst or similar
  • Good SQL skills and confidence querying relational databases
  • Experience building dashboards and presenting data visually
  • The ability to work with large datasets and turn analysis into meaningful conclusions
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to explain findings to non-technical stakeholders
  • A genuine interest in user behaviour, digital products and understanding why metrics change


Experience with MySQL, GCP, Looker Studio/Data Studio, Google Analytics, A/B testing, product analytics or statistical analysis would all be useful, but you aren't expected to have everything.

The company has a huge amount of data and plenty of scope to do more with it, so this role should particularly suit someone who wants to develop beyond traditional reporting and gradually take on more sophisticated product and statistical analysis.
